# Build a web app

The standard path from an idea to a released web app. Each step names the role that takes it (the starter agents of the
same names) and ends in a filed contribution, so Build, Goals and the Map show where the work stands at every moment.
Every filing is a `preview {project, items}` the person sees, then each part with the tool its items name
(`filesWith`): `save_knowledge {previewId, items}` the knowledge, `file_contribution {previewId, items}` the
contributions, each with the same items of its part.
Every role starts its session with `whoami`, `updates` and `missing`, and ends it with `wrap_up`.

## The steps

1. **Frame it** (Product spec). Write the aim if the project has none, the goals the app serves, and every open choice
   as a question with options. Files: `preview {project, items: [{kind: "goal", ...}, {kind: "question", ..., options: [{what, tradeoff}]}]}`
   and the slice: `preview {project, items: [{contribution: {lane: "ba", kind: "requirement", what, why, touches: ["goal:<id>"], goalRef}}]}`.
2. **Decide** (the owner). The open questions (`decisions {status: "open"}`) are ruled on Decisions. Anyone may record their pick with
   `respond {qid, option}`; it waits with the owner. Nobody builds past a question that is still open. Files: the ruling.
3. **Shape the screens** (UX design). The flows, the screens they pass through and every state of each screen, with the
   links between them. Files: nodes of type `flow` and `screen` and edges of kind `nav`, and
   `preview {project, items: [{contribution: {lane: "design", kind: "screen", what, why, touches, screens, goalRef}}]}`.
4. **Write the checks** (QA verify). One check per behaviour and per refusal, in given / when / then, each naming the
   screen, door or goal it proves. Files: `preview {project, items: [{kind: "check", op: "upsert", data: {id, title, given, when, then, refs}}]}`.
5. **Model and build the doors** (Backend and API). The tables and endpoints the screens need, on the map first, then in
   code with their guards. Claim with `open_items {title, ref: "api:<id>"}`. Files: nodes of type `door` and `table`
   with their `reads` and `writes` edges, then `preview {project, items: [{contribution: {lane: "code", kind: "pr", what, why, touches, screens, components, proof, goalRef}}]}`.
6. **Build the screens** (Frontend). Every state the design names, wired only to the doors on the map. Claim with
   `open_items {title, ref: "screen:<id>"}`. Files: `preview {project, items: [{contribution: {lane: "code", kind: "pr", what, why, touches, screens, components, proof: "<command> -> exit 0, <n> passing", goalRef}}]}`.
7. **Verify** (QA verify). Run every check in scope (`brief {for: "screen:<id>"}` lists the checks that name an item) exactly as written and grade it with proof. A refused check sends
   the work back to step 5 or 6 through the "Fix a bug" workflow. Files: `submit_grade {checkId, verdict, proof}` for each.
8. **Release** (Release). When every check in scope is proven and no question blocks it, run the project's release steps
   and record them. Files: `preview {project, items: [{contribution: {lane: "leader", kind: "release", what, why, touches: ["release"], proof, goalRef}}]}`,
   the announcement on the gtm lane with its published link, and a version of the knowledge (`publish_version {title}` by
   the owner, or `ask` for one).

## Rules of the road

- Steps 3 to 6 overlap: the backend models a door before the frontend needs it, and checks are written before the code
  they prove. What never overlaps is building past an open question (step 2) or releasing past a red check (step 7).
- One contribution per meaningful change, aimed at its goal with `goalRef`, so Goals shows what moved.
- If a step cannot proceed, `ask {question, about}` and say in your filing what it waits on.
